clue.text: In Denver drunk staggered about on the left

indicators.note: on the left means placed in front, since English reads from left to right

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
staggered or swayed

explanation.surface: Someone drunk in Denver lurches about on the left side of the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocked is American slang for intoxicated, which is why the clue sets it in a US city.

clue.text: Wave from urchin holding up crown

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece holding up another sits above it, so the crown comes first

parts.note: CR is the abbreviation for crown
a mischievous child

explanation.surface: A street kid lifts up a crown, and some wave comes out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To crimp is to put waves or curls into hair, and a crimp is such a wave.

clue.text: Scots tut over English line which must be toed?

indicators.note: in a down entry, one part placed over another comes first in the column

parts.note: och is a Scottish exclamation of impatience
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A Scot tuts disapprovingly at the English, who must toe the line.
explanation.walkthrough: The oche is the line behind which a darts player stands; 'toe the line' becomes literal.
explanation.definitionFit: In darts the throwing line on the floor must be toed by the player, so it is literally a line to toe.

clue.text: Turn out Chiron, say, onto Gallic street

indicators.note: one part placed onto another simply follows it here

parts.note: Chiron is a small icy body classed as a comet as well as a minor planet
the French word for street

explanation.surface: Chiron the centaur, perhaps, steps out onto a French street.
explanation.walkthrough: Chiron looks like the mythical centaur, but here it is the astronomical object named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that turn out as hoped are said to come true, so the phrases are idiomatic equivalents.

clue.text: Worn-out charger, eg, HRH unplugged in unconscious act

indicators.note: something unplugged is disconnected and taken out, so letters are removed

parts.note: a knacker is an old horse fit only for slaughter; a charger is a horse
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was a royal highness

explanation.surface: An exhausted horse, or the heir to the throne, pulls out a plug without thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives knack as a habitual trick or a skill done instinctively, almost without conscious thought.

clue.text: Engineer lied with a special light manner of speaking

indicators.note: to engineer something is to contrive or construct it, so these letters are rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
a Very light is a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol

explanation.surface: A technician lied about a special lamp in a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A speaker's delivery is their style of utterance, the way the words are put across.

clue.text: Passage is in Porter

indicators.note: one word sitting in another is placed within it

parts.note: porter is a dark beer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A corridor is guarded by a hotel porter.
explanation.walkthrough: Porter looks like a person carrying bags, but it is the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, a kind of passage.

clue.text: In German, one's coming

indicators.note: the letters needed are found in the following words, running across them

parts.note: letters running across the end of the first word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: In German, a sentence announces that someone is arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon means soon or shortly, so something anon is coming before long.

clue.text: Excited suitor toting a pendant

indicators.note: toting means carrying, so one piece holds the other inside it
excited means stirred up and agitated, so the letters are disturbed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An eager young man arrives carrying a pendant to give his sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: A sautoir is a long necklace or chain, usually ending in a hanging ornament or tassel.

clue.text: Yellowish covering which protects trail

parts.note: lute is a clay or cement coating used to seal and protect joints
the track an animal leaves for hounds to follow

explanation.surface: A protective coat of colour keeps a footpath safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Lute here is not the instrument but a sealing paste.
explanation.definitionFit: Lutescent is a botanical term meaning tending towards yellow, from Latin luteus.

clue.text: Eccentricity mostly cut short Nijinsky's movement?

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: e is the mathematical symbol for the eccentricity of a conic
Chambers gives chap as to cut or cleave, so chapped is cut

explanation.surface: A dancer's quirk stops his routine early.
explanation.walkthrough: Nijinsky was a celebrated ballet dancer, and the question mark flags him as one example of who might perform the step.
explanation.definitionFit: An echappe is a ballet step in which the feet spring apart from a closed position, the sort of movement a dancer like Nijinsky made.

clue.text: Again gather a little preliminary work just with its start delayed

indicators.note: a start that is delayed comes later, so the opening letter moves to the end

parts.note: short for reconnaissance, scouting work done beforehand
just in the sense of fair or level

explanation.surface: A team meets once more to do a bit of groundwork, just starting late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' signals a shortened word: recon is the clipped form of reconnaissance.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconvene is to assemble once more after a break, so it means gathering a second time.

clue.text: One at war is hot with sickness at Mons, Earl admitted

indicators.note: something admitted is let in, so it goes inside

parts.note: taken as written
H for hot, as on a tap
mal is French for illness, and Mons is a French-speaking Belgian city
E is an abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: A soldier at the front, burning with fever at Mons, is taken into hospital with an earl.
explanation.walkthrough: Mons evokes the First World War battle, but only signals French. Genesis says of Ishmael 'his hand will be against every man', a man at war with all.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Ishmael was foretold to be a wild man whose hand was against everyone, hence an outcast perpetually in conflict.

clue.text: Tedious daily grind preceding husband's sorrow

indicators.note: preceding means coming before, setting the order of the two parts

parts.note: a rut is a dull fixed routine
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A monotonous daily routine leads to a husband's unhappiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is an archaic word for pity or grief, surviving in ruthless.

clue.text: Move to locate Cicero finally diametrically opposed to Caesar

indicators.note: to move things is to shift them around into new positions

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the orator's name ends in this letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and find Cicero, who stood utterly against Julius Caesar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to Caesar' marks the answer as Latin, as a Roman would say it.
explanation.definitionFit: Toto caelo is Latin for 'by the whole heavens', meaning as far apart as possible, utterly opposed.

clue.text: Char's mate with bit stashed

indicators.note: with followed by stashed means one thing is hidden away inside the other

parts.note: Cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate
bit as the past tense of bite, so ate; stashed means tucked away

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady's friend has a little something hidden away.
explanation.walkthrough: Char looks like a cleaning woman, but it is the British slang word for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Char is British informal for tea, and China tea is a kind of it, so the answer is a specific example.

clue.text: Eg, who penned Tamerlane and its opening?

definitions.text: Eg, who penned Tamerlane and its opening?

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe's first published collection was Tamerlane and Other Poems

indicators.note: an opening is the very beginning, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: its refers to Tamerlane, whose initial is wanted

explanation.surface: A quiz question asking for an example of the writer of Tamerlane.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue defines the answer; read in parts, it builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: Poe, author of the verse work Tamerlane, is an example of a verse writer, hence 'Eg'.

clue.text: Blurted out about one having crested plates?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to plump out is to say something abruptly
Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone blurts out a remark about a person with fancy decorated dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Plates are feet, from rhyming slang plates of meat, and crested means plumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumiped describes a bird with feathered feet, and feathered feet are jokingly crested plates.

clue.text: Ornament's numbers held in check by kitchen police

parts.note: KP is US military shorthand for kitchen duty
the abbreviation for numbers

explanation.definitionFit: A knosp is a knob-like or bud-shaped carved decoration in architecture.

clue.text: Elucidating signal is sent by this dashed refined taste at last

definitions.text: Elucidating signal is sent by this

indicators.note: dashed means smashed to pieces, so the letters are broken up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before

parts.note: final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cultured palate is sent a clarifying signal.
explanation.walkthrough: Elucidating here means giving light, which is what a beacon does.
explanation.definitionFit: A needfire is a fire made by friction, also a beacon, so a lit warning signal comes from it.

clue.text: Who'd surprise someone holding a pistol around line

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one piece goes about the other

parts.note: the official who fires the pistol to begin a race
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone armed with a gun circles a queue, ready to shock people.
explanation.walkthrough: The pistol looks menacing, but it is the race official's.
explanation.definitionFit: A startler is one who startles, that is someone who would give a sudden shock.

clue.text: Sermon about Trump's form to linger stateside

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: SER is a dictionary abbreviation for sermon
an American's spelling of mould, a form; Trump stands for American

explanation.surface: A preacher holds forth about the shape the president's appearance takes, lingering in America.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump is not the subject; he only signals American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To smolder is the US spelling of smoulder, to burn slowly, figuratively to persist or remain hidden.

clue.text: Once Victor's taken off aviatrix could be flying this

definitions.text: Once Victor's taken off aviatrix could be flying this

indicators.note: could be suggests one possible rearrangement of the letters
taken off means removed, so a letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: After her passenger has departed, a female pilot might well be flying this.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition; 'taken off' also suggests an aircraft leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: An air taxi is a small aircraft for hire, just the sort of plane a woman pilot could fly.

clue.text: Victim's close concealing old injury

indicators.note: concealing means hiding something inside

parts.note: mure means to wall in or shut up
dere is an obsolete word for harm

explanation.surface: A wounded person hides an old scar.
explanation.definitionFit: A murderee is the person who is murdered, the victim of a killing.

clue.text: Sheath is round acer that's abloom

parts.note: O is round in shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A protective covering surrounds a maple tree in flower.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany an ocrea is a tubular sheath round a stem formed from stipules.

clue.text: Mason's face is retrospective, possibly tense

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the word runs the other way

parts.note: ever as in 'if it could ever happen'
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A stonemason's expression looks back, perhaps anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a mason's face; read it as the verb, a mason facing a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: To revet is to face an embankment or wall with masonry, a mason's facing job.

clue.text: Refuse in New York behind dispute — new US tip must go

clue.text: Glance over and, God, son beams

D for deus, Latin for god
standard abbreviation

clue.text: Most recent ceremony is what makes some tropical landscapes

a ritual

taken as written

clue.text: Repeatedly rip off Charlie

the same piece again

clue.text: Milton's grievous and no longer sweet

explanation.definitionFit: Chambers records the word in an old sense of hard or grievous, as in Milton, and an obsolete sense of pleasing.

clue.text: Shift in derived declaration of shock

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Have it large or it's to go wild

parts.note: taken as written
